summary: Full backend + frontend testing of GoTurf. 30/30 pytest backend tests passed covering auth (admin/owner/customer login, register, duplicate, /auth/me), public turf discovery (list, search, neighborhood/type/amenity filters, detail, availability, pricing with peak/weekend/package discount), guest booking E2E (create -> contact -> pay -> lookup -> cancel with refund info), overlap 409, review guard for future booking, cancellation penalty unit logic, owner overview/turfs CRUD/bookings-with-payout, admin stats/bookings/owners/disputes/audit-logs/coupons CRUD, 403 for non-admins. Frontend E2E Playwright: Home discovery renders 6+ cards, search filter works, turf profile booking widget shows slots+durations, guest Book now -> Checkout -> Pay (mock) -> Confirmation shows GT reference; all 3 role logins (admin -> /admin, owner -> /owner, customer -> /my-bookings) succeed and dashboards render tables and KPIs; Lookup page has correct fields. No critical issues found.

minor.issue: Uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown'); migrate to lifespan handlers.
Mutating operations use query-string params (?approve=true, ?amount=, ?hold=, ?resolution=, ?suspend=) instead of JSON body — unusual for POST and harder for clients to consume.
Phone comparison is exact-string match (no normalization); a user storing '+233200000000' will not match '0200000000'.
Fetches reviews per-turf in a loop (N+1); fine at 6 turfs but will not scale.

issues: Slot buttons for 22:00/23:00 are partially clipped under the DURATION section at 1920x1080 — minor scrollable overflow but still accessible.

action_items: Optionally normalize phone numbers before storage/lookup for guest booking retrieval.
Consider moving admin POST query-param inputs to request body (consistency).
Migrate @app.on_event to FastAPI lifespan handlers (deprecation warning).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1057 lines — approaching the recommended 700-line split threshold; routes/models/pricing/seed could be modularized.
CORS: allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False is fine for current no-cookie JWT flow but should be reviewed before production.
No rate limiting on /auth/login — brute force protection is absent. (Note: credentials-md playbook mentions lockout after 5 fails, but this app uses JWT Bearer only — no lockout implemented.)
Seed admin update path only re-hashes password if changed, but does not re-create admin if soft-deleted; current behavior is acceptable.
booking_datetimes assumes UTC — correct for Ghana (GMT+0) but hardcoded; add a comment to make it explicit.
/api/bookings/{id}/cancel is unauthenticated and takes no proof of ownership — anyone with the booking id can cancel. Should at least require reference+contact or auth token.
test_credentials: Loaded from /app/memory/test_credentials.md — admin/owner/customer all authenticated successfully.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests created TEST_ prefixed users/turfs/coupons and guest bookings; cleaned up via mongosh after test run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py uses pytest-xdist (installed via pytest.ini likely). Login route in frontend is /auth (not /login). Admin console has 5 tabs, Owner has 3. Guest bookings validated by email domain — email-validator rejects .test TLD so use real-looking domains (.gh, .co) in tests. Payments are mocked at POST /api/bookings/{id}/pay (no real Paystack). Cancellation endpoint is PUBLIC — flag for the main agent to consider auth hardening.
security_notes: POST /api/bookings/{id}/cancel and /api/bookings/{id}/reschedule-request have NO auth check — any client with a booking id can cancel/reschedule. Consider requiring contact match (like lookup) or auth token owning user_id.
